collections.title: Differential Equations · ODE Foundations
assumed_background: Derivatives, elementary functions, algebra; linear algebra for systems.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Worked First-Order Problems and Oscillators
assumed_background: Elementary derivatives and antiderivatives, exponentials, graphs; sine and cosine for the oscillator lecture. No prior dynamical systems or PDE theory.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Fourier Series and Periodic Forcing from Scratch
assumed_background: Elementary calculus, trigonometry, first-order linear ODEs and a forced spring model; no functional analysis, Fourier transform or PDE prerequisites.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Laplace Transforms and Switched Forcing from Scratch
assumed_background: Single-variable integration and integration by parts, exponentials and trigonometry, and elementary first-order initial-value problems; no complex analysis or Fourier transform prerequisites.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Periodic Orbits and Hamiltonian Dynamics
assumed_background: ODE flows, linearization, eigenvalues and stability.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Diffusion, Fronts, and Pattern Formation
assumed_background: Multivariable calculus, weak solutions, energy estimates and spectral reasoning.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Conservation Laws and Viscous Shocks
assumed_background: PDE energy methods, weak/entropy solutions and spectral/ODE methods for profile stability.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Dispersive and Nonlinear Waves
assumed_background: Fourier and Sobolev analysis, energy estimates, local existence and wave propagation.029000 is placed before028000 because the detailed Strichartz estimate supports the critical-wave applications.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Kinetic Transport and Equilibration
assumed_background: Transport, weak formulations and energy/dissipation methods.

collections.title: Differential Equations · Variational Structure and Integrators
assumed_background: Hamiltonian systems, variational calculus and the distinction between a continuous identity and a discrete method.
